title: VPC rollout synthetic health & model-smoke test suite
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create and roll out a reproducible synthetic health-check suite that runs automatically after VPC/private deployments. The suite should verify API readiness, model loadability, and a set of smoke/load scenarios that mimic real customer traffic patterns. It must consume Terraform outputs produced by infra (LB DNS, kube namespace, service account), run against canary nodes first, report metrics into Console dashboards, and trigger remediation playbooks on failure. Deliverables: (1) a test harness in infra/vpc/healthchecks/, (2) Terraform module outputs documented and post-deploy job spec, (3) CI job that runs the suite as part of the after-deploy pipeline, (4) runbook for oncall/SEs with rollback and scale steps.
acceptance_criteria: Post-deploy job can be triggered from CI and uses terraform output variables: lb_address, kube_namespace, model_image_tag, cert_arn
API readiness endpoint (GET /healthz and POST /v1/generate) passes for canary with 0% 5xx for 3 consecutive runs
Model load test: cold start load for catalog standard 13B quant model completes <= 60s in VPC canary, warm start < 10s
Smoke generation: 60s of 25 concurrent short requests (<= 128 tokens) shows error rate < 1% and p95 latency < 400ms
Streaming smoke: 10 simultaneous streaming sessions of 512-token increments maintain stable KV cache (no OOM) and complete within SLOs
Load profile run: 5 minutes at 50 concurrent requests demonstrates sustained throughput without GPU OOM and avg token cost within expected budget
Suite uploads results to Console: test run metadata, token counts, error rates, and links to logs
Automated failure actions: if model load fails twice, trigger canary rollback or scale-up action; if API readiness fails, open incident and post run artifacts to #infra-oncall
test_plan: 1) Pull terraform outputs from infra pipeline artifacts. 2) Deploy canary with rollout policy set to 10% traffic. 3) Run API readiness checks: GET /healthz, GET /metrics, POST minimal generate to validate auth and routing. 4) Run model-load workflow: schedule an empty-run to force model pull, measure load time and memory usage via /internal/metrics. 5) Run smoke generator: short prompts, medium prompts, and streaming sessions. 6) Run bounded load profile for 5 minutes. 7) Validate metrics: error rate, p50/p95 latency, GPU mem usage, KV cache hit rate. 8) Collate outputs and publish results to Console and GitHub artifact store.
implementation_notes:
- New harness lives in infra/vpc/healthchecks/ with a Dockerfile and small Go runner 'vpc-checker'.
- Terraform module will expose outputs: lb_address, kube_namespace, canary_label, cert_arn, service_account_email. Document these in module README.
- Use existing smoke-runner library (github.com/redwood-inference/smoke-runner) and add VPC auth plugin.
- Metrics exported to Console via internal test ingestion endpoint; also push Prometheus metrics to test-run job for Grafana dashboard.
- Secrets: test service account token stored in CI secret manager; ensure least-privilege.
- Failure paths: backoff+retry for transient DNS errors, immediate abort on repeated 5xx from API, trigger rollback via console rollout API.
- Add flag to skip heavy load for small infra (estimate infra cost).
runbook_steps: Trigger post-deploy: CI -> infra/ci/after_deploy_job with parameter run_healthchecks=true
Watch canary logs: kubectl -n ${kube_namespace} logs -l rollout=canary -f
If model load fails: check node GPU memory, check image tag, run 'kubectl describe pod' and fetch /internal/metrics for OOM events
Rollback: use Console rollout API to shift traffic back to previous model variant or call infra rollback playbook (link in Confluence)
Scale up: increase dedicated pool size via infra API or apply terraform patch to bump instance_count and re-run suite
Escalate: post summary and artifacts to #infra-oncall and tag oncall engineer; open incident if customer-facing routes are affected
